text:
maria: hitting a weird edge in the Python SDK when we get a 422 with a validation payload. SDK raises a generic HTTPError but the JSON body is thrown away.
sam: can you paste the payload?
maria: here's the response body we see in prod (redacted):
```json
{"error":{"type":"validation","fields":{"email":"invalid"}},"request_id":"req_01G7XK9"}
```
maria: SDK currently does `raise HTTPError(response.status_code, response.text)` so no structured info and no request_id in exception. hurts debugging.
jordan: oof. we should at least attach parsed json to an attribute on the exception like `.payload` and `.request_id` so callers can introspect.
sam: +1. also for async usage the exception type is raised from the lower-level httpx client, and our wrapper sometimes rewraps into a `ClientError` that loses `__cause__`. makes exception chaining invisible.
maria: repro steps: async call to Client.chat.completions -> 422 -> handler catches and does `raise_from` but body parse fails on unexpected content-type and then we lose raw text too.
infra-ci: looks like a CI test caught a similar case in the sample-apps suite: test expects structured error, got string. filing infra ticket.
sam: proposal: change HTTP error class to `RedwoodHTTPError` with string fields: `message`, `status_code`, `raw_body`, `json_payload`, `request_id`, `headers`. Keep backwards compat by `.args[0]` staying as old message.
jordan: typing-wise we can add a `TypedPayload = Dict[str, Any]` alias and annotate `.json_payload` as `Optional[TypedPayload]` — but keep runtime checks light. also ensure `__repr__` doesn't blow up on big bodies.
maria: for retry logic, we currently retry on 5xx only. product wants a retry on 429 when `retry-after` header present and on 503 transient if `x-retryable: true` header present. we need to expose headers from exception so the caller can implement custom backoff.
sam: agreed. we'll add convenience `should_retry` method on the exception that inspects headers and status_code (simple heuristic). default policy stays unchanged.
jordan: tests: add unit that simulates invalid content-type (text/plain) with JSON-like body to ensure raw_body preserved and json_payload None, not raising parse error. coverage for async and sync code paths.
maria: small example of how app code could use it after change:
```py
try:
    await client.chat.completions.create(...)
except RedwoodHTTPError as e:
    if e.request_id: log.warning('req %s failed', e.request_id)
    if e.json_payload and e.json_payload.get('error'):
        handle_validation(e.json_payload)
    elif e.should_retry():
        backoff_and_retry()
    else:
        raise
```
sam: implementation note: keep parsing tolerant: try json.loads(raw) inside try/except, if it fails store raw as-is. don't call `.decode()` twice for httpx response.
infra-ci: added failing test to CI queue: 1769502468-py-sdk-exception-preserve-raw.test (will run on next PR).
maria: I'll open a small PR with the exception class and tests. tagging @devx-bot for review priority. :eyes:
devx-bot: PR created by maria: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432 - title: `py: preserve error payload & request id in exceptions` - reviewers: sam, jordan.
sam: nice. can we include a migration note in changelog so downstream users know about new attributes?
jordan: yes — add short note under 0.12.4: new `RedwoodHTTPError` attributes and `should_retry()` helper.
maria: thanks all — I'll include a tiny sample-app change to show the pattern. will update once CI green. :thumbsup:
